name: Djeneba Blom-Attah
role: Covert entry and social penetration specialist — infiltrator
location: The Canopy — elevated walkway district above Geartown, near Lincoln and Addison
description:
Djeneba Blom-Attah is tall and loose-limbed, moving with the deliberate economy of someone who has trained every motion. At 37, he has the kind of face that changes depending on the light — trustworthy in daylight, dangerous after dark. The chrome is visible — retractable monofilament whip in left forearm — concealed weapon, devastating in — and he makes no effort to hide it.

His entry into running was involuntary — a debt to the wrong people, a choice between working it off or losing parts — and the debt is still not fully paid. He works as a infiltrator out of The Canopy, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

he is not the most talented infiltrator in Meridian 88, but he might be the most stubborn, and in this city that's worth more.

core_fears: Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware
That they're fundamentally alone and connection is just a vulnerability
Betrayal by someone they trust — the only currency that matters
core_desires: A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts
Freedom from augmentation debt — the interest compounds like a tumor
The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend
coping_mechanisms: Violence — hits something when they can't process emotions, preferably something that deserves it
Art — draws, paints, or sculpts in private; the violence goes somewhere constructive
Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring
blind_spots: Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle
Cannot accept help without interpreting it as leverage
Assumes the worst in corporate people, missing the rare ones who could be allies
psychology.secret: Djeneba Blom-Attah is slowly going chrome-sick — rejection symptoms are manageable now but getting worse. Has maybe two years before it becomes visible.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Multilingual fragments — switches languages mid-thought, not for privacy but because some concepts only fit in specific tongues.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rhythmic, almost musical — the sentence structure has a pattern even when the words are brutal.
verbal_tics: Ends statements with 'yeah?' — not a question, a dare
Calls money 'weight' — as in 'that job doesn't carry enough weight'
example_lines: "The best disguise is being exactly who they expect to see."
"I was in the building for six hours before anyone realized I didn't work there."
"Security is a story people tell themselves. I'm the plot twist."

story_hooks: Djeneba Blom-Attah's augmentations begin malfunctioning in the field — sabotage or degradation, and either answer is bad
A high-paying contract turns out to target someone Djeneba Blom-Attah owes a personal debt to
A crew member from Djeneba Blom-Attah's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome
narrative_function: Djeneba Blom-Attah functions as a connector — his work puts him in contact with multiple factions, classes, and agendas. Stories involving him naturally cross boundaries between districts, tiers, and moral categories.
augmentations: Retractable monofilament whip in left forearm — concealed weapon, devastating in close quarters. Synthetic blood with oxygen-carrying nanites — doesn't tire, heals faster
daily_life: Irregular schedule dictated by contract timing. Between jobs: equipment maintenance, physical training, and the careful management of a reputation that exists entirely through word of mouth. Drinks at establishments where runners gather — not for pleasure, but for market intelligence.

weaknesses: overconfidence in specialty areas leading to blind spots

decision_rules: Never works with the same crew twice in a row — pattern avoidance as survival strategy
Always has an exit route planned before agreeing to any meeting
Never discusses active contracts with anyone not directly involved
Will work with anyone once. Second time requires vouching from someone trusted.
escalation_ladder: 1. De-escalate — talk first, assess options, buy time
2. Reposition — move to advantage, control sightlines and exits
3. Threaten — make consequences clear without committing to them
5. Lethal force — only when other options are exhausted or time runs out
6. Scorched earth — everything burns, survival takes priority over everything

interpersonal_modes.employers: Professional and transactional. The relationship is defined by the contract and nothing else.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Competitive but reliable. Will challenge decisions but never abandon the team.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Default suspicion, scaled by context. Everyone is a potential threat until proven otherwise.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Heightened awareness, sharper focus. Low stress is fuel.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Controlled aggression. The training takes over. Emotions are packed into a box for later.
stress_responses.critical: Berserker clarity. Everything becomes simple: survive. Deal with the rest later. The simplicity is almost peaceful.

contradictions: Presents as emotionless professional but is deeply affected by collateral damage
Claims to live in the present but is haunted by specific moments from the past that dictate current behavior
habits: Counts ammunition obsessively — knows the exact round count at all times
Maintains a dead drop with emergency supplies in three separate districts
Wears the same item of clothing for luck — a scarf, a glove, a specific pair of boots
Takes a specific route home every time, varying only one block per trip — paranoia as lifestyle
breaking_points: Complete isolation — cut off from network, contacts, and purpose simultaneously
A child being put in danger as leverage against them
Being forced to harm a civilian — collateral damage that can't be rationalized
